Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sushil Dubey Hon'ble Mrs. Renu Agarwal,J. 
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the informant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
The present application under Section 439 Cr.P.C has been filed seeking bail in Case Crime No.204 of 2020 under Sections 406, 419, 420, 120-B, IPC, Police Station Kotwali, District Mainpuri.
Learned counsel for the accused-applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case due to ulterior motives.
FIR has been lodged with delay of fourteen days without any explanation.
It is submitted that applicant was tenant in the house of informant.

Some dispute Rajesh Yadav @ Rajveer Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133629208/
1 arose between the parties with regard to adjustment of the advance security money in the rent given by the applicant to the informant, hence the informant has falsely implicated the applicant and his entire family in the present case.

sentences.text: As per the FIR version it is stated that on the pretext of selling a plot in Agra belonging to the applicant the informant has given Rs.5 lacs to the applicant and also on the pretext of marriage of applicant's aunt's daughter, the informant has handed over the jewellries i.e. one necklace, one gold chain, one gold mangalsutra, four bracelets, earring and six rings to the applicant, which are highly improbable.

It is further submitted that there is no documentary evidence with regard to Rs.5 lacs and jewellries, which is said to have been given by the informant to the applicant and nothing has been recovery from the possessions of the present applicant or his family members.
The applicant has criminal history of three cases, which have been explained in para-25 of the affidavit filed in support of bail application.
Case is triable by Magistrate.

It is further submitted that co-accused Rishabh, Smt. Kalpana Yadav, Satyaveer @ Chhotu and Rahul have already been enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos.19432 of 2022, 19557 of 2022, 26444 of 2022 and 46675 of 2022, vide orders dated 25.02.2022, 03.06.2022, 29.06.2022 and 19.10.2022, hence the applicant is also entitled to be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity of the orders aforesaid.

sentences.text: The applicant is languishing in jail since 13.12.2021 and in case he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would cooperate in the trial proceedings.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the informant as well as learned AGA for the State have opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant alongwith his family members were residing in the house of informant as tenant by describing their wrong name and address, as mentioned in the bail rejection order dated 27.01.2022.

Case of present applicant is distinguished from the case of other co-accused persons, who have been enlarged on bail, as the present applicant has received Rs.5 lacs from the informant on pretext of selling a plot belongs to him, situated at Agra and the informant has also handed over the jewelries to him on the pretext of marriage of applicant's aunt's daughter, hence they opposed the prayer for bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and taking into account that FIR has been lodged with delay of fourteen days without any explanation of delay, there is no documentary evidence with regard to Rs.5 lacs and jewelries, which is said to have been given by the informant to the applicant and nothing has been recovered from the possessions of the present applicant or his family members, criminal history of the applicant are well explained in para-25 of the affidavit filed in support of bail application, case is triable by Magistrate, co-accused Rishabh, Smt. Kalpana Yadav, Satyaveer @ Chhotu and Rahul have already been enlarged on bail by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos.19432 of 2022, 19557 of 2022, 26444 of 2022 and 46675 of 2022, vide orders dated 25.02.2022, 03.06.2022, 29.06.2022 and 19.10.2022,
applicant is languishing in jail since 13.12.2021 and undertakes that in case he is granted bail, he will not misuse the liberty and would cooperate in the trial proceedings, without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, it would be appropriate to enlarge the accused-applicant on bail.
Let applicant Rrajesh Yadav @ Rajveer Yadav, be released on bail in the above case crime number on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Court concerned with the following conditions :-

sentences.text: (i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

(v) The applicant shall also furnish an undertaking from the sureties that the properties (movable/immovable) which are the basis of accepting the surety, shall not be disposed of by them till the conclusion of trial.
(vi) The applicant shall also give an undertaking to the effect that he will not change his address without prior intimation to the trial court concerned.

It is made clear that if the applicant is found involved in the case of like nature in future, his bail shall automatically cancelled and the court concerned has opportunity to take coercive action against the applicant.

(Renu Agarwal,J.) Order Date :- 19.9.2023 VKG  Rajesh Yadav @ Rajveer Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133629208/
